collection: IELTS Academic and General Training Speaking Part 1 practice
note: Three original familiar-topic clusters with illustrative spoken models and practice rubrics. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Speaking
questions.learningObjective: Respond to familiar interview questions with relevant personal information and clear spoken detail.
questions.prompt: Who do you usually send short messages to during the day?
questions.answer: Mostly my younger brother. We leave home at different times, so I send him quick messages about things like who has the house key or whether someone has collected a parcel.
questions.explanation: Original illustrative response, not a required life story or the only acceptable position. Assess the candidate’s own spoken language across the interaction. The written model does not demonstrate pronunciation, fluency or a verified speaking duration.

markingGuide.description: Fluency/coherence in the actual spoken response: sustained, logically connected development earns 2; uneven development or frequent disruptive hesitation earns 1; no assessable connected speech earns 0. Natural pauses are acceptable.
Lexical resource in speech: appropriate range with effective paraphrase earns 2; limited or sometimes inappropriate choices earn 1; too little intelligible language to assess earns 0.
Grammatical range/accuracy in speech: varied structures with generally clear meaning earn 2; a narrower range or errors sometimes obscuring meaning earn 1; largely unassessable language earns 0.

Pronunciation from live speech or recording only: intelligible phrasing, sounds and stress without undue listener effort earn 2; recurring difficulty that requires effort earns 1; largely unintelligible or no spoken evidence earns 0. Do not score this from a transcript or require imitation of a particular national accent.
